input: Declutter and donate my digital photo duplicates

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The size and location of the photo library (phone, cloud, hard drive, multiple devices) determines the tools needed and the complexity of the task.
Whether the photos are personal-only or shared with family/others affects what can safely be deleted and what needs coordination before donating.
Whether 'donate' means contributing to a stock/archive platform, sharing with a charity, or something else entirely changes the workflow significantly.
A hard deadline or available time window determines how thorough the process can be and whether automated tools are necessary.
The user's tolerance for automation vs. manual review affects which duplicate-detection approach to recommend — some people want to approve every deletion.
Knowing what 'done' looks like — e.g., zero duplicates, a target storage size freed, or a specific number of photos donated — shapes how thorough the process needs to be.
The operating system and tools already available (Mac, Windows, Google Photos, iCloud, etc.) directly determines which duplicate-finder tools can be used.

gold.taskTitle: Declutter and donate digital photo duplicates
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find, remove, and donate duplicate photos from their digital collection.

questions.title: Where are your photos stored right now?
questions.description: Identify all locations holding the photo library — e.g., iPhone, Android, external hard drive, Google Photos, iCloud, Dropbox, or a mix of these.

questions.title: Are these photos shared with anyone else?
questions.description: Determine if others (family members, friends, colleagues) have access to or co-own parts of the library, which affects what can be deleted without coordination.

questions.title: What does 'donate' mean to you here?
questions.description: Clarify the intended donation target — for example, a public photo archive, a stock photography platform, a local charity, or gifting prints/files to family.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline or time limit for this?
questions.description: Find out if there is a specific date the task must be completed by, or a total number of hours available, which shapes how automated or manual the approach should be.

questions.title: Do you want to approve each deletion or automate it?
questions.description: Establish the user's comfort level with automated duplicate removal versus manually reviewing and confirming every photo before it is deleted.

questions.title: What would a successful outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Define the finish line — e.g., a specific amount of storage freed, zero remaining duplicates, a target number of photos donated, or simply a tidy, organised library.

questions.title: What device and operating system will you use?
questions.description: Identify the primary device (Mac, Windows PC, iPhone, Android) and any apps already installed, so the right duplicate-detection tools can be recommended.
